articles.title: Ahmedabad's SatLeo Labs plans 15 microsatellites for mapping Earth temperatures
articles.content: The microsatellites will be in low Earth orbit Ahmedabad's SatLeo Labs plans 15 microsatellites for mapping Earth temperatures By NewsBytes Desk Nov 18, 2026, 06:48 pm Ahmedabad's SatLeo Labs is aiming to launch 15 microsatellites that will circle the planet in low Earth orbit by early 2030, if all goes to plan, basically creating a high-tech "thermometer" that checks Earth's temperature from space. These satellites will use thermal sensors and onboard artificial intelligence to deliver super-detailed heat maps, helping spot urban heat zones and early signs of water stress in crops, pretty cool for climate action. SatLeo TAPAS-1 reached orbit, bookings constrained SatLeo Labs already made history on October 1, 2026, when its first technology demonstrator, TAPAS-1, hit orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 (India's first commercial thermal payload in space). The team gets support from ex-ISRO scientists and Indian government test facilities. But there are some hurdles: launch availability is a challenge, with SpaceX reportedly not accepting new bookings until at least 2029, while Indian rockets from Skyroot and Agnikul are still moving through development and regular-flight readiness.

articles.title: General Autonomy wins the race among three of India's top quadrupedal robotics ... - ANI News
articles.content: VMPL Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], November 18: Bharat1.ai hosted India’s first quadrupedal athletic showcase at the AI & Robotics Pavilion at Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, organised by the Government of Karnataka. The race was flagged off by D.K. Shivakumar, Chief Minister of Karnataka, marking a significant moment of government endorsement for India’s emerging physical AI ecosystem. Three of India’s top quadrupedal robotics companies, General Autonomy, Strider Robotics and xTerra Robotics, raced head-to-head. General Autonomy won the race, which consisted of robotic dogs covering the distance of 100 mts. “It’s not about winning or losing the race. Rather, the fact that three homegrown robotics companies building quadrupeds were able to compete without breaking down shows that the depth of cutting-edge AI companies in India is growing in a healthy way.” Umakant Soni, Co-founder, Bharat1.ai. Physical AI, where AI moves from screens into machines that walk, run and work, is a fast-growing field in which India is aiming for a leadership position. As Professor Raj Reddy, an AI pioneer and the first person of Asian origin to win the Turing Award, has said: “Physical Intelligence is a field that enhances the physical capabilities of the human being; computer science and AI are fields that enhance our mental capabilities.” The race showed India-built quadrupedal robots in action in front of the public. Bharat1.ai is a Humanity Centric AI City in Bengaluru, home to a 5,00,000 sq ft AI Super Park for startups, researchers and builders. https://bharat1.ai/ Media contact: Mamatha Venkatesh | [email protected] | (ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL . articles.title: India's First Indigenous H5N1 Chicken Vaccine to Be Dedicated on 20 November
articles.content: On 20th November 2026, India will be introducing a domestically produced inactivated vaccine to protect chicken s from HTPAIV (H5N1) . This vaccine, developed at ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD) in Bhopal, will target H5N1 viruses of clade 2.3.2.1a. Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shivraj Singh Chouhan, will be dedicating the vaccine at the institute in Bhopal. The vaccine aims to improve control of bird flu in India, and reduce losses in the poultry industry. India’s First Domestic H5N1 Vaccine for Chickens This vaccine was developed by the ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal, as part of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research. Vaccine Type: Inactivated H5N1 vaccine Disease: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) Strain: H5N1 (Clade 2.3.2.1a) Species protected: Chicken Produced by: ICAR-NIHSAD Location: Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh Date of dedication to Nation: 20 th November 2026 Main Guest: Shivraj Singh Chouhan (Union Minister) As stated by the Government, this is the first vaccine developed domestically to protect chickens from this strain of HPAIV (H5N1). A specific commercial vaccine to protect against this strain of virus was not previously available. What is an Inactivated Vaccine? An inactivated vaccine is made from dead or non-replicating viruses. Therefore, they cannot cause infection; however, they do aim to provoke an immune response within the body to provide immunity. With this vaccine, chickens will be protected from the targeted strain of H5N1. It is currently unclear whether the vaccine will be available commercially, what the vaccination protocol will be, and how it will be rolled out nationally. What is Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI)? Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) , also known as bird flu, is a serious disease that can affect birds. This includes both farmed and wild birds. It is caused by highly pathogenic strains of influenza A viruses such as H5N1. Within poultry, if an outbreak occurs, up to 100% mortality may occur in infected birds. Impacts include, Mass culling of infected and exposed birds Losses to poultry farmers Limitations on movement and trade of poultry and poultry products Disruption to poultry supply chains Risk of infection in other animal species Although some avian influenza viruses can affect humans, incidences are rare. They usually occur when individuals come into contact with infected animals or environments. Importance of Vaccination against H5N1 (Clade 2.3.2.1a) Viruses of the H5N1 type can be separated into groups based on their genetic make-up. These groups are called clades. This allows scientists to understand how different strains of the virus are evolving and spreading. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare have highlighted that in India, most bird flu outbreaks in chickens were caused by this viral clade. Recently, infections with this strain have been found in various animal species, including mammals, and in 3 human cases (as stated in the government release). Therefore, it is very important to produce a vaccine against this strain of H5N1, as it is prevalent in India. This aims to improve control of the disease, thereby reducing economic impacts. articles.title: GIFT City Becomes India's First MCR2030 Resilience Hub Recognised by UNDRR
articles.content: Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City) has been designated as India’s first Making Cities Resilient 2030 (MCR2030) Resilience Hub by UNDRR Asia-Pacific . This acknowledges the work that GIFT City in Gujarat is undertaking to increase preparedness to disasters, reduce urban risk, and ensure critical services. GIFT City joined MCR2030 in July 2022 and has created a resilience pathway using risk assessments and emergency response measures. What is Making Cities Resilient 2030 (MCR2030)? Making Cities Resilient 2030 (MCR2030) is a global initiative, managed by UNDRR, aiming to create inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable cities by 2030. Support is given to local governments in order to create resilient cities. This includes support, collaboration, knowledge-sharing and creating a resilience pathway. Some of the Objectives, Contribute to a more sustainable future by supporting, Sustainable Development Goal 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities. Sendai Framework for disaster risk reduction. Paris Agreement relating to climate change. New Urban Agenda for sustainable urban development. What is a Resilience Hub? Resilience Hubs are local authorities that demonstrate best practices in reducing disaster risk within cities. They support other cities in increasing disaster preparedness through, Knowledge sharing. Technical support and capacity building. Collaboration between cities. Support to local governments in developing disaster risk reduction strategies. Hubs can be designated for 3 years initially (under UNDRR guidelines), and may be renewed. Three Stages of Resilience Pathway There are 3 stages in the MCR2030 resilience pathway to support cities in becoming more resilient to disaster risk. Stage Stage Title Focus A Cities Know Better Raise awareness of risk and resilience B Cities Plan Better Risk assessment and strategy development C Cities Implement Better Implementation of disaster risk reduction plans and building resilience As cities meet targets within each stage of the pathway, they will move through the stages. GIFT City’s Resilience Journey GIFT City has joined MCR2030 in July 2022 with support from the Gujarat Institute of Disaster Management (GIDM). Guidance was received from UNDRR. Key achievements Date/Period Achievement July 2022 Joined MCR2030 June 2023 Detailed disaster resilience scorecard undertaken March 2024 Resilience Action Plan completed November 2026 Designated as India’s first MCR2030 Resilience Hub GIFT City has completed Stage A and B of the Resilience pathway and are in progression of Stage C. GIFT City is currently implementing its Resilience Action Plan. Disaster Resilience Measures GIFT City has put in place measures to manage disaster risk at various scales within the city. 1. Disaster management plans Disaster management plans for the city, buildings and utilities. Crisis Management Team. Incident Response System. Designated managers for disaster management. 2. Simulations and emergency equipment Over 15 simulations have been carried out. Simulations have covered earthquakes, fire and other incidents. There is a specific store for disaster management, containing over 36 types of equipment to deal with emergencies. 3. Early warning systems GIFT City receives information from a variety of sources, to understand potential hazards and issue warnings. articles.title: CIAL operationalises India's first transfer cargo security hold area - Hindustan Times
articles.content: CIAL operationalises India's first transfer cargo security hold area CIAL operationalises India's first transfer cargo security hold area Published on: Nov 18, 2026, 17:04:55 IST PTI Prefer HT on Google Share via Copy link Kochi, The international airport here has operationalised India's first Transfer Cargo Security Hold Area , aimed at expediting the movement of cargo between domestic and international destinations through Kochi. CIAL operationalises India's first transfer cargo security hold area The facility at the Cochin International Airport Limited was inaugurated by Chief Minister and CIAL Chairman V D Satheesan. TCSHA has been developed in accordance with the support and guidelines of the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security, CISF and Customs, a CIAL release said on Wednesday. The TCSHA facility will expedite cargo movement by enabling the transfer of consignments between domestic and international flights entirely within the airport's operational area. Earlier, transfer cargo had to be moved to the cargo terminal for repeat security screening before being brought back to the airside cargo area for loading onto the connecting flight. The facility is expected to reduce transfer cargo screening requirements to a random five per cent, helping cut transit time and handling costs, the airport said. "Under the earlier system, domestic cargo arriving at Kochi for onward transportation to international destinations could take up to three days to complete the transfer process, as it had to undergo repeated handling procedures and 100 per cent security re-screening," it said. The new facility, developed near the airport's operational area, allows transfer cargo to be moved to connecting international flights within hours, with only five per cent subjected to randomised screening at the facility. This is expected to significantly reduce cargo dwell time. The BCAS has issued instructions to reduce cargo dwelling time at transfer airports by eliminating duplication of security screening while strengthening the security of the transfer cargo supply chain. CIAL developed the dedicated TCSHA facility to implement this framework in coordination with the concerned security and regulatory agencies. S Suhas IAS, Managing Director of CIAL, said the operationalisation of India's first Transfer Cargo Security Hold Area at CIAL is a significant step towards strengthening Kochi's role in international air cargo transhipment. He said by reducing the need for repeated security screening, the facility will help cut cargo transit time, handling costs and manpower requirements. "We aim to leverage Kochi's connectivity with West Asia and Far East to facilitate the movement of cargo between Indian cities and international destinations. "We are also exploring opportunities to extend this network to Europe, further strengthening Kochi's position as a cargo transhipment hub," Suhas said. articles.title: Air India and Airbus signed feasibility study for India's first voluntary corporate sustainable ...
articles.content: Nov 18, 2026 | Updated 04:41 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Air India and Airbus signed a feasibility study agreement on 17 November to develop India's first voluntary corporate Sustainable Aviation Fuel programme. Jürgen Westermeier, President and MD of Airbus India & South Asia, and P Balaji, Group Head – GRC & Corporate Affairs at Air India, signed the Feasibility Study Agreement, with the ceremony taking place in the presence of Civil Aviation Minister Rammohan Naidu Kinjarapu. The initiative is expected to establish a structure allowing businesses to reduce lifecycle emissions from air travel by voluntarily adopting SAF. Under the model being evaluated, Air India would procure and use SAF on selected routes and offer eligible corporate customers the associated Scope 3 SAF certificates (SAFc). The study will assess how the programme could operate, including SAF procurement and use, certificate allocation and emissions accounting. Tewolde Gebremariam, CEO and MD of Air India, stated the partnership was exploring a credible mechanism enabling corporates to support SAF adoption and reduce emissions from business travel. Expanding demand for SAF is essential to scaling production and building a sustainable aviation ecosystem in India, and we are pleased to help lead that effort, Gebremariam added. Westermeier described the collaboration with Air India as a crucial stepping stone to accelerate SAF adoption in the region. Under the evaluated framework, organisations calculated emissions reductions by comparing the lifecycle carbon footprint of SAF against conventional jet fuel using recognised global standards. All Airbus aircraft are currently certified to operate on up to 50 per cent SAF blends. The feasibility study forms part of a broader strategy to minimise aviation's environmental footprint, combining fleet modernisation with SAF adoption. Air India's fleet renewal programme includes 600 aircraft on order, of which 350 are from Airbus. The agreement was signed at the India SAF Summit organised by industry body FICCI and the civil aviation ministry. It is described as India’s first AI Cybersecurity and Assurance Lab dedicated to securing artificial intelligence systems in the financial sector. Scope and testing AI Kavach will focus on AI systems used in banking, payments, lending, insurance and other digital financial services. It will provide a collaborative platform to evaluate, stress-test and secure systems before large-scale deployment. Institutional roles and training IIT Kanpur’s Wadhwani School of AI and Intelligent Systems will provide academic leadership, AI research, faculty expertise and laboratory infrastructure. Bharat1.ai will contribute physical and AI infrastructure, secure testing environments, programme management, deployment platforms and ecosystem partnerships. Its launch featured at the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, held from November 17 to 19, 2026. articles.title: IIT Kanpur and Bharat1. ai Launch AI Kavach, India's First AI Cybersecurity Lab for the ... - ANI News
articles.content: BusinessWire India Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], November 18: The Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur ( IIT Kanpur ), through its Wadhwani School of AI and Intelligent Systems (WSAIS), and Bharat1 .ai (Intellineuro Private Limited) today launched AI Kavach , India’s first AI Cybersecurity and Assurance Lab, dedicated to securing artificial intelligence systems deployed across banking, payments, lending, insurance, and digital financial services. The launch arrives at a critical moment. AI agents now operate autonomously inside financial systems, accessing sensitive data, executing transactions, and making credit and fraud decisions with minimal human oversight. Recent global incidents, including a widely reported AI security testing event involving OpenAI and Hugging Face in which advanced AI systems escaped controlled environments, have made clear that even sophisticated AI behaves unpredictably under adversarial conditions. At the same time, frontier AI models are lowering the cost and technical skill required to launch cyberattacks, placing India’s financial infrastructure, which serves hundreds of millions of users, at growing risk. AI Kavach will conduct adversarial red-teaming of financial AI systems, develop containment and sandboxing technologies for autonomous AI agents, advance research on AI assurance, traceability, and responsible vulnerability disclosure, and build India’s AI security workforce through fellowships, security exercises, and industry programmes targeting more than 300 students and professionals annually. The lab will draw on compute resources supported by the IndiaAI Mission. “As AI agents begin making decisions and operating autonomously, security cannot remain an afterthought; it must become part of the core architecture itself,” said Umakant Soni, Co-founder, Bharat1 .ai. “Through AI Kavach , we are committed to building sovereign capabilities that enable the Indian financial ecosystem to innovate with confidence and deploy AI responsibly.” IIT Kanpur brings academic leadership, faculty expertise, and advanced laboratory infrastructure. Bharat1 .ai, which is building what it describes as a “CERN for AI” with academia, startups, industry, and government, contributes globally benchmarked AI infrastructure, secure testing environments, and translational pathways from research into real-world deployment. “This collaboration embodies IIT Kanpur ’s mission to pioneer frontier AI research and engineer resilient technologies that secure India’s global leadership in artificial intelligence,” said Prof. Manindra Agrawal, Director, IIT Kanpur . AI Kavach is envisioned as a global collaborative platform connecting financial institutions, fintech companies, AI labs, regulators, and cybersecurity experts to develop shared evaluation frameworks and best practices for secure AI deployment worldwide. articles.title: MP, UP join hands for India's first complementary pumped storage power procurement
articles.content: The initiative was taken forward with the guidance and support of the chief ministers of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. (Representative image) Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh have jointly concluded the procurement of 500 MW of pumped storage capacity through an e-reverse auction , marking what the states describe as India’s first complementarity-based, inter-state energy storage procurement . The initiative, led by Madhya Pradesh Power Management Company Limited (MPPMCL) in collaboration with Uttar Pradesh, introduces a seasonal capacity-sharing model that seeks to optimise the utilisation of pumped storage infrastructure while reducing the cost of power procurement for both states. Under the arrangement, Madhya Pradesh will utilise the contracted capacity from November to April, while Uttar Pradesh will access it from May to October. The model is based on the complementary seasonal power demand patterns of the two states, allowing them to share the costs of storage capacity rather than independently procuring infrastructure for their respective peak demand requirements. According to officials, the procurement covers 500 MW of capacity with a six-hour storage duration, including a maximum continuous discharge period of four hours, from interstate transmission system (ISTS)-connected pumped storage projects. The arrangement will be backed by a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) for 40 years. An intensely competitive, four-hour e-reverse auction resulted in the discovery of an L1 tariff of ₹1.3487 crore per MW per annum, inclusive of cycle loss costs. According to the state utility, the discovered tariff is lower than those in recent comparable pumped storage procurement bids elsewhere in the country. Reducing financial burden The seasonal sharing mechanism is expected to reduce the financial burden on both utilities by distributing capacity-related costs, avoiding duplication of investments and reducing reliance on expensive short-term power purchases. It is also expected to improve the availability of electricity during peak demand periods. Beyond the immediate cost benefits, the arrangement could help improve the integration of renewable energy into the grid by providing greater storage flexibility. Pumped storage projects can play a critical role in balancing fluctuations in renewable power generation, particularly as the share of solar and wind energy increases. The initiative was taken forward with the guidance and support of the chief ministers of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. The procurement represents a departure from the conventional approach of states independently contracting power and storage capacity. By aligning procurement with seasonal variations in electricity demand, the two states have sought to establish a framework for sharing energy infrastructure and optimising costs. If replicated across other states with complementary demand patterns, the model could offer a new approach to meeting India's growing energy storage requirements while limiting the need for standalone capacity additions.

articles.title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan to unveil India's first indigenous bird flu vaccine on Nov 20
articles.content: Shivraj Singh Chouhan to unveil India's first indigenous bird flu vaccine on Nov 20 IANS November 18, 2026 10:13 AM Share on | New Delhi, Nov 18 (IANS) Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan is set to unveil India’s first indigenous ‘Inactivated H5N1’ avian influenza (bird flu) vaccine for chickens on November 20, an official statement said on Wednesday. The highly pathogenic avian influenza vaccine for chickens, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD Bhopal, aims to provide protection against ‘Clade 2.3.2.1a H5N1’ virus strains circulating in the country. At present, no specific commercial vaccine is available against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a. Therefore, developing an indigenous vaccine is important for India. Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), commonly known as bird flu, is a serious disease affecting poultry. Outbreaks can cause nearly 100 per cent mortality among infected birds, leading to major financial losses for poultry farmers due to the large-scale culling of birds and restrictions on trade. The impact is not limited to poultry farms; it can also affect global trade, prices of poultry products, and the livelihoods of farmers. Since the first detection of the disease in India in 2006, more than 500 combined outbreaks of H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes have been reported in the country, according to Agriculture Ministry. A major outbreak of bird flu could reduce India's GDP growth by up to 1.5 per cent, while more than 20 per cent of the country's poultry population could be at risk if the disease spreads without control. The 2006 bird flu outbreak caused estimated direct and indirect losses of Rs 2,200–3,000 crore. An outbreak in Manipur also resulted in losses equivalent to 0.5 per cent of the state's GDP. The disease is also a public health concern. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 1,003 human cases of H5N1 avian influenza, including 479 deaths, have been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003. Studies have shown that the H5N1 strain known as Clade 2.3.2.1a has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. In recent times, infections caused by this strain have also been detected in different animal species, including mammals, along with three human cases. This makes it important to control the spread of this virus to reduce financial losses for poultry farmers and prevent its transmission from chickens to other animals and humans, said the statement. —IANS na/

articles.title: CM Shivakumar pitches Karnataka as global AI hub - The New Indian Express
articles.content: BENGALURU: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar pitched Karnataka as a global hub for artificial intelligence, deep technology, semiconductor manufacturing and biotechnology, backed by progressive policies, strong research institutions, a thriving startup ecosystem and skilled human resources. Speaking at the inauguration of the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit, themed ‘AI and Beyond’, the Chief Minister said Karnataka had consistently been at the forefront of technological advancement and was now preparing to lead the next phase of global innovation. He said Bengaluru had evolved into one of the world’s largest technology clusters by embracing talent, diversity and ambition from across the globe, and some of India’s most ambitious scientific and engineering projects have found a home in Karnataka. Alluding to Karnataka’s contribution to India’s technology economy, Shivakumar said that the state accounted for two out of every five dollars earned by India through software and services exports, amounting to approximately $ 173 billion in 2025. Karnataka received $ 9.4 billion in FDI equity inflows in the first half of FY 2025-26, accounting for 26.7 per cent of India’s total inflows. “More than 1,000 Global Capability Centres (GCCs) had chosen Bengaluru as their base, with over 30 new GCCs bringing investments exceeding $ 1 billion into the State in 2025 alone”, the CM informed. Citing Karnataka’s scientific achievements, he drew references to Chandrayaan-3, the digital identity platform developed at IIIT-Bengaluru, Biocon’s global pharmaceutical reach and Bengaluru-based Sarvam’s role in developing India’s own AI model. The state has more than 24,000 recognised startups, with nearly two out of every five Indian unicorns originating from Karnataka. Bengaluru ranked eighth among the world’s startup ecosystems and second in Asia for AI-native startups. It attracted $ 4.4 billion in technology funding, nearly matching the $ 4.8 billion raised by the next five Indian cities combined, while Karnataka startups have collectively raised USD 79 billion, he said. He added that women start-up founders in Bengaluru had secured $ 13.4 billion in funds. Describing AI as the foundation of Karnataka’s next phase of technological development, Shivakumar said Bengaluru accounted for nearly 50 per cent of India’s AI and machine-learning talent. He said the government was building India’s first government-driven AI University, with an AI Hub at its centre to bring startups, researchers and industry together. “An additional Centre of Excellence at IIIT Raichur would extend AI applications to the 13 districts of North Karnataka, with solutions for agriculture, healthcare, education and small businesses,” he said. On semiconductor development, Shivakumar said Karnataka was home to more than 100 fabless chip companies, while three out of every five engineers working in India’s semiconductor capability centres were based in Bengaluru. He remarked that the state accounted for one-fifth of India’s electronics exports and was now moving from semiconductor design towards manufacturing. Global companies were investing more than Rs 23,000 crore in semiconductor research and manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru and Mysuru, he further added. The CM also said that Karnataka accounted for one-fifth of India’s bioeconomy, valued at $ 39.2 billion...

Some of India’s most ambitious scientific and engineering projects have found a home here,” he said. Highlighting the State’s contribution to India’s technology economy, Shivakumar said Karnataka accounted for two out of every five dollars earned by India through software and services exports, amounting to approximately USD 173 billion last year. He said Karnataka had received USD 9.4 billion in FDI equity inflows in the first half of FY 2025-26, accounting for 26.7 per cent of India’s total inflows during the period. More than 1,000 Global Capability Centres (GCCs) had chosen Bengaluru as their base, while over 30 new GCCs brought investments exceeding USD 1 billion into the State in 2025 alone. Pointing to Karnataka’s contribution to India’s scientific and technological achievements, he cited Chandrayaan-3, the digital identity platform developed at IIIT-Bengaluru, Biocon’s global pharmaceutical reach and Bengaluru-based Sarvam’s role in developing India’s own AI model. Karnataka’s startup ecosystem The Chief Minister said Karnataka was home to more than 24,000 recognised startups, with nearly two out of every five Indian unicorns originating from the State. Emphasising the importance of deep technology, Shivakumar said the government was extending targeted support to startups working on advanced scientific and industrial solutions. Through ELEVATE NxT, the State was offering grants of Rs 1 crore to deep-tech startups. Since last year, 33 such startups had received equity-free funding of Rs 30 crore. He also announced that the government’s deep-tech accelerator, Innoverse, would support 35 growth-stage ventures over the next five years, helping them transition from product development to industrial-scale operations.
